terms.meaning: a lookup table that converts a reading status into a timeline severity level
a database option that returns only one row per value, here one reading per vital type

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in route tools, audit and timeline services, database access and the vital sign input formats.
sections.why: Needed to save readings, log them and add timeline events.

sections.name: VitalsController (part 1)
sections.title: Recording a vital sign reading
sections.what: Saves a reading for the signed-in user with its type, values, unit, status and source, defaulting to normal and manual entry. It logs the creation and builds a readable title such as the type and value with unit.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond keeping the record and a readable title.
sections.watch_out: The default of normal means a reading sent without a status is shown as fine.

sections.name: VitalsController (part 2)
sections.title: Timeline entry for the reading
sections.what: Adds a timeline event for the reading with a severity mapped from its status, and returns the saved reading.
sections.why: Likely reason: readings should appear in the health history with a warning level.
sections.watch_out: A missing status falls back to mild severity, so an unclassified reading is not flagged.

sections.name: VitalsController: if
sections.title: Listing readings with filters
sections.what: Returns the user's readings newest first, filtered by type and date, with paging details, and logs the view.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond showing history in pages.
sections.watch_out: The filter object is loosely typed, so a new filter must be added carefully.

sections.name: VitalsController (part 4)
sections.title: Latest reading per type and deleting
sections.what: The latest route returns the newest reading for each vital type and logs the view. Delete removes one of the user's readings and logs it only if something was removed.
sections.why: Lets the home screen show current values without loading full history.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is permanent here, and the latest route does not show whether a reading was later deleted.

summary: Lets a signed-in user record, list, view the latest reading for each type, and delete their own vital sign measurements.
purpose: Stores readings such as blood pressure, heart rate and blood sugar, and shows them on the timeline.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Storing each reading lets the app draw trends over time.
how: Create saves a reading with its status and source, audits it and adds a timeline event with a mapped severity. List returns readings with filters and paging. Latest returns the most recent reading per type. Delete removes one reading owned by the user and logs it.
inputs: CreateVitalSignDto and QueryVitalsDto values, the reading id from the URL, and the user id from the token.
outputs: Objects with success and data, paging details for lists, or a deleted count result.
risks: Delete is permanent. The status defaults to normal when not given, so an unchecked reading is recorded as normal.
debug: If a reading is missing, check its userId and measuredAt. If the timeline severity looks wrong, check the severity map. If the latest route is slow, check the database index on type and time.
